entries.clue: Pedal-pumped reed instrument that stood in for pipes in small chapels
Its Latin name likens it to a ship; it runs east from a church's west door
Choral service at dusk; cathedrals sing it daily and visitors may drop in free
Big name whisked through a private entrance, well away from the crowds
Of the great plates whose grinding builds mountains and shakes cities
Underwater peak that never quite grew tall enough to break the waves
'I believe' in Latin, sung after the Gospel in a choral Mass
Trundle slowly along the ground on wheels, engines idling
Panels let down from the back of a wing to give lift at low speed
Sicilian giant that regularly dusts Catania with grey powder
Melted rock still down in the depths, waiting for a way to the surface
Wide open hall in which travellers mill about before setting off
